content.text:
Confirmed. Cluster 2 vs B cells gives CD3D (logFC 6.0), CD3E, IL32, CD7, IL7R, GIMAP7, NOSIP — unambiguous T-cell lineage.

## What I ran

All work was done on **usegalaxy.org** (Galaxy 26.1) in a new history, **"PBMC3k scRNA-seq clustering + cell typing 2026-11-04"** (`bbd44e69cb8906b52581b3d1be6b5eef`). Input: `pbmc3k_raw.h5ad` (dataset `f9cad7b01a4721353e80471331aef932`), which `Inspect AnnData` showed to be **2700 cells × 32738 genes, `var: 'gene_ids'`** — the standard 10x PBMC 3k raw matrix.

Pipeline (ebi-gxa **scanpy-scripts 1.9.3** tool suite, one Galaxy job per step):

| Step | Tool | Result (from job stdout) |
|---|---|---|
| QC filter cells | Scanpy FilterCells | `n_genes` 200–2500, `pct_counts_mito` ≤ 5 → **2638 × 32738** |
| Filter genes | Scanpy FilterGenes | `n_cells` ≥ 3 → **2638 × 13656** |
| Normalize | Scanpy NormaliseData | CPM→10,000 + log1p (`uns: 'log1p'`), saved to `.raw` |
| HVG | Scanpy FindVariableGenes | seurat flavour → **2638 × 2000** |
| Scale | Scanpy ScaleData | zero-centre, clip at 10 |

Top markers per cluster (Wilcoxon, all adjusted p ≤ 5e-6; marker table hid 15):

- **0** — LDHB, LTB, **CD3D**, **CD3E**, IL32, **IL7R** → CD4⁺ T
- **1** — **S100A8/S100A9**, **LYZ**, TYROBP, **FCN1**, CST3, LGALS2 → CD14⁺ monocytes
- **2** — only ribosomal genes + MALAT1 (see below) → CD4⁺ T
- **3** — **CD79A**, **CD79B**, **MS4A1**, CD74, HLA-DRA/DQA1, **TCL1A**, VPREB3, LINC00926 → B
- **4** — **CCL5**, NKG7, **GZMA**, **GZMK**, **CD8A**, CST7, CTSW, PRF1, KLRG1 → CD8⁺ T
- **5** — **FCGR3A (CD16)**, LST1, FCER1G, AIF1, **CD68**, SERPINA1, CFD, SPI1 → FCGR3A⁺ monocytes
- **6** — **GNLY**, **NKG7**, **GZMB**, **PRF1**, **FGFBP2**, **SPON2**, CD247, FCGR3A (no CD3D) → NK
- **7** — **FCER1A**, **CLEC10A**, HLA-DPA1/DPB1/DQA1, CD74, CST3 → dendritic cells (cDC2)
- **8** — **PPBP**, **PF4**, **GP9**, SDPR, GNG11, NRGN, RGS18, SPARC → platelets/megakaryocytes

**On cluster 2** (the one soft call): against *all other cells* its only markers are ribosomal proteins and MALAT1. Two targeted comparisons resolved it — vs cluster 0 it differs *only* by ribosomal/MALAT1 content at trivial effect sizes (logFC 0.09–0.42, hid 17), i.e. no lineage difference; vs cluster 3 (B cells) it is strongly CD3D⁺ (logFC 6.0), CD3E⁺, IL32⁺, CD7⁺, IL7R⁺, plus naive-associated NOSIP and GIMAP7 (hid 19). So clusters 0 and 2 are one CD4⁺ T compartment that Leiden splits at res=1.0 along a ribosomal-content/naive-vs-memory axis, not two distinct cell types.

Two caveats on the pipeline as run: `FindVariableGenes` applied its default `n_top_genes=2000`, which in scanpy supersedes the min_mean/max_mean/min_disp cutoffs I passed, so HVGs are the top 2000 by normalized dispersion. I did not regress out `total_counts`/`pct_counts_mito` (an optional tutorial step); it does not affect these lineage assignments.
